title: Virginia: Approval of State Coal Combustion Residuals Permit Program
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) is approving Virginia's coal combustion residuals (CCR) permit program under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). After reviewing the CCR permit program application submitted by the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (VADEQ), EPA has determined that Virginia's partial CCR permit program meets the standard for approval under RCRA. Virginia's CCR permit program will operate in lieu of the Federal CCR program with the exception of the specific provisions noted below.

title: Neostellar Capital Corp., et al.
Utah Underground Injection Control Program; Class VI Primacy
summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) has received a complete Underground Injection Control (UIC) program revision application from the State of Utah, requesting primary enforcement responsibility (primacy) for Class VI injection wells under Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) section 1422. The EPA's approval of the State's UIC program revision application would allow the Utah Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration. In this action, the EPA proposes to approve Utah's application to implement the UIC program for Class VI injection wells located within the State, except those on Indian lands for which the EPA retains primacy. The EPA has determined that Utah's UIC Class VI program meets Federal requirements for primacy under SDWA section 1422 and the applicable implementing regulations in 40 CFR parts 144, 145, and 146.

title: Regulatory Considerations for Prescription Drug Use-Related Software; Guidance for Industry; Availability
summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance for industry titled "Regulatory Considerations for Prescription Drug Use-Related Software." This final guidance describes FDA's application of its drug labeling authorities to certain software outputs that are disseminated by or on behalf of a drug sponsor for use with a prescription drug product or a prescription drug-led, drug-device combination product that is assigned to the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research or the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research as the lead center. This guidance finalizes the draft guidance of the same title issued on September 19, 2023.

title: Notification to Members/Shareholders
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage.

title: Privacy Act of 1974; System of Records
summary: In accordance with the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB or Bureau) proposes to modify a current Privacy Act System of Records Notice (SORN) titled, "CFPB.001--Freedom of Information Act/Privacy Act System." This modification clarifies the purpose of the SORN, the categories of records and individuals, the legal authorities, the system manager, the system location address, and the records retention schedule, and introduces a new routine use to permit the disclosure of records to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) or other Federal agencies for records inspection purposes.

title: Nonconforming Investment Special Reserve
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is proposing to amend its regulations governing the requirements for federal share insurance. This action would remove the requirement for federally insured, state-chartered credit unions to establish a special reserve for certain investments that are beyond those authorized for federally chartered credit unions. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary compliance and administrative burdens for state-chartered insured credit unions without diminishing the agency's ability to protect the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund.

title: Conversion to State-Chartered Credit Union
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to remove a regulatory provision regarding the process for maintaining federal share insurance following the conversion of a federal credit union (FCU) to a state charter. The provision is unnecessarily duplicative of a similar provision contained in NCUA's Chartering and Field of Membership Manual (Manual), and is outdated, having been superseded by amendments to the Manual.
